column2: net: Support SO_REUSEPORT sockets with bpf_sk_assign

column1: Currently the bpf_sk_assign helper in tc BPF context refuses SO_REUSEPORT
sockets. This means we can't use the helper to steer traffic to Envoy
which configures SO_REUSEPORT on its sockets. In turn
from removing TPROXY from our setup.
The reason that bpf_sk_assign refuses such sockets is that the
bpf_sk_lookup helpers don't execute SK_REUSEPORT programs. Instead
one of the reuseport sockets is selected by hash. This could cause
dispatch to the ""wrong"" socket:
sk = bpf_sk_lookup_tcp(...) // select SO_REUSEPORT by hash
bpf_sk_assign(skb
Fixing this isn't as simple as invoking SK_REUSEPORT from the lookup
helpers unfortunately. In the tc context
column2: L2 headers are at the start

column1: of the skb
column2: while SK_REUSEPORT expects L3 headers instead.

column1: Instead
column2: we execute the SK_REUSEPORT program when the assigned socket

column1: is pulled out of the skb
column2: further up the stack. This creates some

column1: trickiness with regards to refcounting as bpf_sk_assign will put both
refcounted and RCU freed sockets in skb->sk. reuseport sockets are RCU
freed. We can infer that the sk_assigned socket is RCU freed if the
reuseport lookup succeeds
column2: but convincing yourself of this fact isn't

column1: straight forward. Therefore we defensively check refcounting on the
sk_assign sock even though it's probably not required in practice.
